## 1. Email reply to Jane

**Subject: Planning your parental leave and 2026 benefits**

Hi Jane,

Congratulations, and thank you for reaching out early. The handbook page you found is out of date. **The policy effective July 1, 2025 replaces that section:** it provides up to **16 weeks of paid parental leave at 100% of base pay** for employees with at least six months of continuous service on their first day of leave.

You reached six months on **September 3, 2025**, so you meet that service requirement for leave beginning around your **February 16, 2026** due date. You do not need to rely only on PTO and unpaid leave.

Here are answers to your questions, using February 16 as a planning start date.

### 1. Can you carry over 10 PTO days?

**No—the carryover limit is five unused days.** PTO accrues at 1.25 days per completed calendar month, credited at month-end. Because you started March 3, March was not a completed calendar month of service.

| Calculation | Days |
|---|---:|
| April–October: 7 completed months × 1.25 | 8.75 |
| Less PTO used in 2025 | −4.00 |
| Calculated balance as of November 3 | **4.75** |
| Expected November–December accrual: 2 × 1.25 | +2.50 |
| Projected December 31 balance, before forfeiture | **7.25** |
| Maximum carryover into 2026 | **5.00** |
| Amount forfeited if you use no more PTO in 2025 | **2.25** |

This projection assumes normal accrual through December and no additional PTO use. To avoid losing the projected 2.25 days, please discuss taking them before year-end with your manager.

The supplied policies do not explain whether PTO can be attached to parental leave or whether PTO continues accruing during leave. HR will confirm those points before we finalize your schedule.

### 2. Can you increase your Dependent Care FSA now?

**Pregnancy alone does not provide a stated basis for a mid-year change in the benefits guide.** Mid-year changes are allowed only within 30 days after a qualifying life event, including birth.

The **2026 household limit is $7,500**. If your baby arrives on February 16, the 30-day change deadline would be **March 18, 2026**; the actual deadline will depend on the actual birth date.

For setting up a higher election *before* the birth, our Benefits team will confirm the 2026 annual-enrollment dates, election rules, and effective date. Those details are not in the supplied guide. Please do not assume your current $1,000 election can be increased immediately.

### 3. Do you have to tell your manager now?

The current policy says employees **should give 30 days’ notice when leave is foreseeable**. For a February 16 start, that means notice by **January 17, 2026**. Waiting until early January would fit that timing; waiting until the end of January would not.

The policy does not specify whether notice must go directly to your manager or whether a separate manager-notification deadline applies. HR will confirm the required recipients and process so you know when you need to involve your manager. If your planned leave starts earlier, the notice target also moves earlier.

### 4. Is your job protected?

**NY Paid Family Leave provides up to 12 weeks of job-protected leave.** Based on your full-time schedule and continuous employment since March 3, you completed its 26-week eligibility period on **September 1, 2025**.

For New York employees, company parental leave runs at the same time as NY PFL—not after it. The company pays the difference between the NY PFL benefit and 100% of base pay.

**FMLA is different:** it requires both 12 months of service and 1,250 hours worked in the preceding 12 months. You will not meet the service requirement on February 16; your first anniversary is **March 3, 2026**. HR, with Legal, will verify your hours and whether FMLA protection can begin during an ongoing leave.

Importantly, the supplied materials **do not establish job protection for all 16 company-paid weeks**. For illustration, a continuous 16-week leave starting February 16 would run through **June 7**, with a June 8 return. The first 12 weeks would run through **May 10**. HR and Legal will confirm protection for the remaining period rather than assume paid leave automatically guarantees it.

You may take company parental leave in up to **two blocks of at least two weeks each**, within 12 months of the birth. Please send HR your tentative start date and whether you prefer one continuous leave or two blocks. We can then confirm the outstanding details and help you build a leave plan.

Warmly,  
HR  
Northwind Freight Systems, Inc.

## 2. Internal note to the HR policy owner

**Subject: Parental-leave source corrections and gaps**

The intranet still displays superseded Handbook §7.2 (12-month eligibility/12 weeks paid). Replace it or prominently link PB-2025-04, effective July 1, 2025 (six months/16 weeks), and align employee-facing materials.

Please clarify:

- Job protection during company-paid weeks beyond NY PFL’s 12 weeks.
- FMLA eligibility reached mid-leave, hours verification, and coordination with company leave/NY PFL.
- Notice recipients, submission process, and whether “should give 30 days’ notice” is advisory or mandatory.
- PTO attachment to leave and accrual during leave.
- Dependent Care FSA annual-enrollment dates, election effective dates, and birth-related change procedures.

Ask Legal to validate the leave-protection guidance and Benefits to supply enrollment instructions. Jane’s case needs confirmation of protection beyond the initial 12 weeks; paid-leave eligibility alone should not be presented as a job-protection guarantee.
